title: Integrated Transcriptome-Metabolome Analysis of Rps2-A226Y Mutant Liver
text:
This post summarizes an integrated liver omics analysis in female mice carrying Rps2-A226Y, comparing mutant versus wildtype at two corrected ages: 9 months and 15 months.
The workflow combines differential transcriptomics and metabolomics to identify pathway-level progression across time, with emphasis on bile acid metabolism, oxidative stress, lipid remodeling, and protein quality control pathways.

title: Integrated Transcriptome-Metabolome Analysis of Rps2-A226Y Mutant Liver
text:
Main Biological Takeaways

The mutant phenotype is progressive from 9m to 15m across both omics layers.
Bile acid pathway dysregulation strengthens with age and remains a dominant signature.
Stress-adaptation programs appear stronger earlier, with altered regulatory balance later.
Lipid and antioxidant pathway changes support age-dependent metabolic remodeling.
Most strongly significant features preserve direction across time, with selective switches.
Sphingomyelin species accumulate broadly, consistent with a chain-length-dependent ceramide synthase (Cers2/Cers4) shift toward the SM-conversion arm of the pathway.
Lysosomal genes, especially cathepsins, are broadly downregulated alongside XIAP upregulation, consistent with a lysosome-linked anti-apoptotic adaptation.
Pre-ranked GSEA (fgsea + MSigDB) independently recovers bile acid metabolism and proteasome/protein-degradation signatures among the top pathways.
Gene-metabolite concordance is not uniform across pathways: some (amino acid, purine/pyrimidine) agree in direction, while bile acid and lipid pathways show more disagreement worth further investigation.
A database-driven enrichment cross-check (SMPDB via MetaboAnalystR) is only weakly informative here: roughly 20% of measured metabolites appear in SMPDB, and that subset is biased against lipids. Correcting the statistical background from the pathway library to the measured metabolome weakens every contrast by about an order of magnitude, leaving no FDR-significant pathway at either age.
What remains is a nominal, uncorrected tendency toward depletion of TCA-adjacent intermediates and carnitine at 9 months, driven by a small overlapping metabolite set.

title: About Ivan
text:
Hi!
This is my personal blog about my profession and hobbies. Currently I am specializing on computational biology and data science in biomedical research conducting a postdoc project at Novartis. My gate computer languages are R and bash, but I also have some experience with Python as well as with html and other relevant tools like Quarto, Github and AI assistants. My biological background spans through several major areas currently converging on cell and molecular biology, systems biology and omics. I am highly interested in understanding tissue regeneration through mitigating the inflammation and fibrosis as well as other aspects of cell signaling and senescence.
In my free time I prefer to learn how to program, foreign languages, listen to and play music on guitar. I do yoga daily and try to hike outside of my town every month. Besides acquiring hard skills I develop soft skills through participation in Toastmasters meetings, local Ski and Mountain club and occassionally writing blog posts.
My passion is transforming clinical and biological data into actionable insights by exploratory analyses, challenging biological hypotheses and performing data visualization. For further details on this please visit my Github and LinkedIn profiles.

title: Mounting the Beast: A DIY Guide to Installing a Beastmaker 1000 Hangboard
text:
Every climber reaches a point in their journey where they look at the empty space above their bedroom door and think: “I could put a hangboard there.”
This is the story of how that thought became a reality, turning a blank wall into a finger-strength training station. Here is the step-by-step saga of mounting a Beastmaker 1000 Series hangboard above a concrete door frame.


Step 1: The Blank Canvas
It all starts with a dream and a blank wall. The space above a doorway is ideal because it allows your legs and body to hang freely, but it is also a high-stress area. You cannot simply screw a hangboard directly into the plaster; you need a solid plan to anchor it safely.



The empty wall above the doorway—full of potential, but currently blank.





Step 2: The Foundation (Metolius Backing Board)
To avoid tearing down the wall and to distribute the forces evenly, we use a wooden backing board (in this case, a Metolius mounting board). This board is anchored securely into the solid wall structure, providing a stable, flat surface to screw the Beastmaker into.



The pre-drilled Metolius backing board, waiting to bridge the gap between the wall and the hangboard.





Step 3: Unboxing the Beast & Preparing the Power
With the backing board ready, it was time to open the main event: the Beastmaker 1000. Alongside the beautiful wooden board, I dug out my trusty Texmash TDU-1000 impact drill. A solid drill is non-negotiable when dealing with concrete or brick walls.



Unboxing the Beastmaker and prepping the Texmash TDU-1000 drill.





Step 4: Organizing the Arsenal
DIY projects live and die by preparation. I gathered the essential tools for the job: * A LUX-TOOLS 40 cm spirit level (crucial—nobody wants to train on a slanted board). * A utility knife for opening packages and clean cuts. * A masonry drill bit matching the anchor size. * A screwdriver and selection of screws.



Gathering the essential tools for a precise installation.





Step 5: Choosing the Right Anchors
When hanging your body weight (plus dynamic force) off a wall, cheap drywall screws won’t cut it. I opted for Fischer S 8x40 wall plugs (8mm diameter, 40mm depth) and matching heavy-duty black wood screws.

[!TIP] Always check the packaging recommendations. For the Fischer S 8x40, a hole depth of at least 50mm and an 8mm drill bit are required for maximum load capacity.




Fischer S 8x40 wall plugs and heavy-duty screws—the unsung heroes of this project.





Step 6: Making the Holes
With the backing board held up and leveled, I marked the drilling points. Then came the noisy, messy part: drilling the 12 anchor holes. You can see the neat little piles of concrete dust resting on top of the door frame, a testament to the Texmash’s impact mode.



Twelve clean holes drilled above the door frame. Measure twice, drill once!





Step 7: Inserting Anchors & Preparing Screws
Next, the Fischer wall plugs were tapped into the holes, and the long black screws were started. Having the screws partially inserted in the wall beforehand makes aligning and mounting the heavy wooden backing board much easier.



The screws aligned and ready to catch the backing board.





Step 8: Securing the Backing Board
The backing board is up! It went on smoothly and was screwed tight until it was completely flush with the wall. A quick check with the spirit level confirmed everything was perfectly horizontal.



The Metolius backing board is securely mounted and leveled.





Step 9: Unleashing the Beastmaker
Finally, the moment of truth. The Beastmaker 1000 was aligned on the backing board and screwed in using the wood screws provided. The wood-on-wood mount is incredibly strong and looks fantastic.



The finished setup: The Beastmaker 1000 is ready for training.


With the board solid as a rock, it was time to chalk up and test the 35-degree slopers. Let the training sessions begin!
